docs.title: Welcome to fme-mcp-ultra
docs.text: fme-mcp-ultra is the universal, open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Safe Software FME 2025.2, geospatial data, enterprise data pipelines, and AI agents.

docs.title: 🎯 Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• FME 2025.2 Support: Complete support for local FME Form via CLI and in-memory fmeobjects bindings, alongside remote FME Flow REST APIs.
  • Automated Workspace-to-Tool Generation: Dynamically inspects .fmw workspaces, extracts published parameters, and exposes them as strongly validated MCP tools.
  • Enterprise DevSecOps: Hardened by default with directory containment (PathGuard), command injection protection (CommandGuard), outbound network defense (SSRF Guard), and automated PII / credential scrubbing.
  • MCP Federation: Native client capabilities emulating and expanding upon FME 2026's MCPCaller.
  • Geospatial Intelligence: Built-in spatial vector algorithms (reprojection, buffering, geometry repair), dataset profiling, and data contracts.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
Explore our guides to install, configure, and integrate fme-mcp-ultra with your favourite MCP client:

  • Installation Guide

  • MCP Client Setups
  • Security Model
  • Tools Catalogue

docs.title: Authentication & Authorisation
docs.text: fme-mcp-ultra supports multiple enterprise authentication and authorisation mechanisms to ensure that all tool operations are properly governed.

docs.title: A. Static API Key
docs.text:
Configured via FME_MCP_AUTH_MODE=api_key and FME_MCP_API_KEY=<token>. In HTTP transport mode, clients must pass the token in the Authorization header: 

Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>
Or via the X-API-Key header: 
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

docs.title: B. OAuth 2.1 / OIDC
docs.text:
In enterprise environments, fme-mcp-ultra integrates with standard OAuth 2.1 identity providers (Keycloak, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID) using JWT Bearer tokens: 

Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
Tokens are validated for expiration, audience, issuer, and cryptographic signature.

docs.title: C. FME Flow Token Forwarding
docs.text: When communicating with FME Flow, the server forwards client-provided or environment-configured FME Flow tokens (fmetoken token=...) directly to the FME Flow REST endpoints.

docs.title: 2. Authorisation (RBAC & ABAC)
docs.text:
Access to tools is strictly governed by the Role-Based Access Control (RBACEngine) and Attribute-Based Access Control policy layer:

Role Authorised Tool Prefixes platform_admin * (All tools) tenant_admin fme_, data_, gis_, raster_, cad_, quality_, catalog_, workflow_, mcp_, ai_, gov_, util_ workspace_operator fme_run_, fme_get_, fme_list_, fme_search_, fme_stream_, data_, gis_, util_ spatial_analyst gis_, raster_, cad_, data_read_, data_profile_, fme_get_, fme_list_, util_ data_analyst data_, quality_, catalog_, fme_get_, fme_list_, util_ auditor gov_audit_, gov_list_, catalog_get_, fme_get_job, quality_get_, util_ read_only fme_get_, fme_list_, data_read_, catalog_get_, util_

Any request to invoke a tool outside the user's role raises a SecurityError with code FORBIDDEN.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
All settings can be configured via environment variables (prefixed with FME_MCP_), a .env file, or command-line parameters.

Variable Default Description FME_MCP_HOST 0.0.0.0 Host address to bind HTTP/SSE server FME_MCP_PORT 8000 Port for HTTP/SSE transport FME_MCP_TRANSPORT stdio Transport mechanism (stdio or streamable-http) FME_MCP_LOG_LEVEL INFO Logging verbosity (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR) FME_ALLOWED_DIRS Current working directory Semicolon-separated file-system allowlist for PathGuard FME_ALLOWED_OUTBOUND_DOMAINS safe.com,github.com Whitelist for outbound federation calls (SSRF Guard) FME_DIR Auto-detected Local FME Form installation directory FME_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 600 Maximum execution timeout for workspaces FME_FLOW_URL None Base URL of enterprise FME Flow instance FME_FLOW_TOKEN None Bearer token for FME Flow REST authentication

docs.title: Contributing to fme-mcp-ultra
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to fme-mcp-ultra! We welcome contributions from geospatial specialists, software engineers, security researchers, and data practitioners worldwide.

docs.title: Code Standards & Guidelines
docs.text:
1. Language & Spelling: All code comments, docstrings, documentation, commit messages, and PR descriptions must use British English (en-GB) (e.g. optimise, serialise, colour, catalogue, behaviour).
  2. Type Annotations: Every function and method must be fully type-hinted and pass mypy --strict.
  3. Linting & Formatting: We use ruff for formatting and linting.
  4. Testing: All new tools and security guards must include corresponding unit tests in tests/unit/ and integration tests where appropriate. Minimum test coverage requirement is 85%.
  5. Security First: Input validation, path traversal guards (PathGuard), and command guards (CommandGuard) must be strictly applied on all parameter inputs.

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository on GitHub: https://github.com/mwjouini/fme-mcp-ultra.
  2. Clone your fork locally: 
    git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/fme-mcp-ultra.git
cd fme-mcp-ultra
  3. Install dependencies in an isolated virtual environment: 
    python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"
  4. Run the automated test suite: 
    pytest tests/ -v
  5. Create a descriptive feature branch: 
    git checkout -b feat/add-spatial-cluster-tool
  6. Commit changes with Conventional Commits (e.g. feat(spatial): add DBSCAN clustering tool).
  7. Push to your branch and submit a Pull Request against main.

docs.title: Deployment Overview
docs.text:
fme-mcp-ultra can be deployed across several topologies depending on your operational requirements:

  1. Local Desktop Stdio Mode: Directly coupled with AI clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Antigravity on a workstation with local FME Form installed.
  2. Containerised Streamable HTTP Server: Deployed via Docker or Kubernetes adjacent to an enterprise FME Flow cluster or spatial database.
  3. Hybrid Gateway: Operating in front of both local developer workstations and shared cloud FME Flow instances.

docs.title: Deployment Architectures
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Workstation["Developer Workstation"]
        Client1["Claude Desktop / Cursor"] --> |stdio| LocalServer["fme-mcp-ultra (Local)"]
        LocalServer --> FMEForm["FME Form 2025.2 (fme.exe)"]
    end

    subgraph EnterpriseCloud["Enterprise Cloud / Kubernetes"]
        Client2["Enterprise AI Copilots"] --> |HTTPS / SSE| CloudServer["fme-mcp-ultra (Pod)"]
        CloudServer --> FMEFlow["FME Flow Engine Pool"]
        CloudServer --> PostGIS["PostGIS / Spatial DB"]
    end

docs.title: Docker Deployment Guide
docs.text:
fme-mcp-ultra is packaged as an OCI-compliant container image published on GitHub Container Registry:

docker pull ghcr.io/mwjouini/fme-mcp-ultra:latest

docs.title: 1. Interactive Container Run
docs.text:
To run the containerised MCP server exposing Streamable HTTP on port 8000:

docker run -d \
  --name fme-mcp-ultra \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -e FME_MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable_http \
  -e FME_MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
  -e FME_MCP_PORT=8000 \
  -e FME_MCP_API_KEY="your-strong-api-key" \
  -e FME_FLOW_URL="https://fme-flow.internal.acme.org" \
  -e FME_FLOW_TOKEN="fme-flow-api-token" \
  -v fme_data:/data \
  ghcr.io/mwjouini/fme-mcp-ultra:latest

docs.title: 2. Multi-Container Orchestration with Docker Compose
docs.text:
A standard docker-compose.yml is provided at the repository root:

version: "3.8"

services:
  fme-mcp:
    image: ghcr.io/mwjouini/fme-mcp-ultra:latest
    container_name: fme-mcp-ultra
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    environment:
      - FME_MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable_http
      - FME_MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - FME_MCP_PORT=8000
      - FME_MCP_API_KEY=${FME_MCP_API_KEY:-dev-secret-key}
      - FME_FLOW_URL=${FME_FLOW_URL:-}
      - FME_FLOW_TOKEN=${FME_FLOW_TOKEN:-}
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
      - ./audit:/var/log/fme_mcp
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/healthz"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3

Start the stack with:

docker compose up -d

docs.title: 3. Hardened Security Compose Profile
docs.text:
For production and high-compliance environments, run with docker-compose.security.yml which applies: - Read-only root filesystem (read_only: true). - Dropped Linux capabilities (cap_drop: ALL). - No privilege escalation (no-new-privileges:true). - Non-root user uid: 10001. - Ephemeral writable /tmp tmpfs.

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.security.yml up -d

docs.title: FME 2025.2 Compatibility Strategy
docs.text: Safe Software FME 2025.2 (FME Form Build 25810 and FME Flow 2025.2) lacks native out-of-the-box MCP server support. fme-mcp-ultra bridges this gap through coordinated local and remote adapters:

docs.title: 1. Local FME Form Execution
docs.text:
• Subprocess CLI Runner: Calls C:\Program Files\FME\fme.exe with structured --MACRO_NAME value arguments.
  • In-Memory C-Extension (fmeobjects): Loads fmeobjects.cp310-win_amd64.pyd dynamically via os.add_dll_directory, allowing sub-second querying of published parameters, labels, types, and defaults via FMEWorkspaceRunner.

docs.title: 2. Remote FME Flow REST Integration
docs.text:
• Authenticates via Bearer tokens (fmetoken token=...).
  • Submits asynchronous jobs to /fmerest/v3/transformations/submit.
  • Retrieves execution logs from /fmerest/v3/transformations/jobs/id/{job_id}/log.
  • Polls job lifecycle status until completion.

docs.title: FME 2026 Parity & Transcendence Strategy
docs.text: Safe Software announced and released official Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations starting with FME 2026: 1. FME 2026.1: safe.mcp / MCPCaller on FME Hub (Client mode, allowing FME to call external MCP tools). 2. FME 2026.2: FME Flow Native MCP Server (Server mode, exposing workspaces as MCP tools).

docs.title: ⚖️ Parity Matrix
docs.text:
fme-mcp-ultra implements both modes simultaneously in a single, unified runtime:

Capability FME 2026 Official fme-mcp-ultra Server Mode (Expose Workspaces) ✅ Flow Only (2026.2+) ✅ Form (Local) & Flow (Remote) Client Mode (MCP Caller) ✅ Via Hub Package ✅ Built-in Federation Client Streamable HTTP Transport ✅ Yes ✅ Yes (FastAPI/Starlette) Standard I/O (stdio) Transport ❌ Flow is HTTP only ✅ Yes (Local desktop clients) Directory Sandboxing (PathGuard) ⚠️ Basic permissions ✅ Strict PathGuard & Canonicalisation Command Injection Guard ⚠️ Standard OS ✅ Strict Binary Whitelisting SSRF Network Protection ❌ Not included ✅ Pre-DNS IP Resolution Check PII & Credential Redaction ❌ Not included ✅ Automated Real-Time Masking Built-in Vector GIS Tools ❌ None (must create FMW) ✅ Built-in spatial intelligence Data Contracts & Scoring ❌ None ✅ YAML Data Contracts & Profiling Support for FME 2025.2 ❌ Requires 2026+ ✅ Native 2025.2 support

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: fme-mcp-ultra can be executed locally, installed via pip, run with uvx, or deployed as an enterprise container.

docs.title: 1. Using uvx (Fastest, No Install Required)
docs.text: uvx fme-mcp-ultra serve --transport stdio

docs.title: 2. Using pip
docs.text:
pip install fme-mcp-ultra

Verify your installation and local FME Form environment: 

fme-mcp-ultra doctor

docs.title: 3. Using Docker Container
docs.text:
Run in unprivileged non-root mode:

docker run -d \
  --name fme-mcp-ultra \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -e FME_MCP_TRANSPORT=streamable-http \
  ghcr.io/mwjouini/fme-mcp-ultra:latest

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide describes how to deploy fme-mcp-ultra in production Kubernetes clusters (EKS, GKE, AKS, OpenShift, or on-premises k8s).

docs.title: Manifest Architecture
docs.text:
The k8s/ folder contains production-ready manifests:

  • namespace.yaml: Isolated namespace fme-mcp.
  • configmap.yaml: Non-sensitive application configuration and allowed paths.
  • secret.yaml: Encrypted FME Flow tokens and MCP API keys.
  • deployment.yaml: Replicated Deployment with resource requests/limits, health probes, and security contexts.
  • service.yaml: ClusterIP service exposing port 8000.
  • networkpolicy.yaml: Zero-trust network policy restricting ingress and egress traffic.

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text:
Deploy using kubectl:

# 1. Create the dedicated namespace
kubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yaml

# 2. Deploy ConfigMap and Secrets
kubectl apply -f k8s/configmap.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/secret.yaml

# 3. Deploy Workload & Networking
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/service.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8s/networkpolicy.yaml

docs.title: Pod Hardening & Security Context
docs.text:
Every container runs under strict non-root policies:

securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 10001
  capabilities:
    drop:
      - ALL
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

docs.title: Scaling & High Availability
docs.text:
Because fme-mcp-ultra is stateless in Streamable HTTP transport mode, horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) can be enabled based on CPU utilisation or JSON-RPC request volume:

apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: fme-mcp-ultra-hpa
  namespace: fme-mcp
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: fme-mcp-ultra
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 75

docs.title: MCP Client Integration Guide
docs.text: Step-by-step configuration for leading Model Context Protocol clients.

docs.title: 1. Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Locate your configuration file: - Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json - macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json - Linux: ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

Add the following block: 

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fme-mcp-ultra": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["fme-mcp-ultra", "serve", "--transport", "stdio"],
      "env": {
        "FME_DIR": "C:\\Program Files\\FME",
        "FME_ALLOWED_DIRS": "C:\\Program Files\\FME;E:\\fme_mcp"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 2. Cursor IDE
docs.text: In Cursor Settings (Features -> MCP Servers), add: - Name: fme-mcp-ultra - Type: command - Command: fme-mcp-ultra serve --transport stdio

docs.title: 3. Antigravity
docs.text:
In your Antigravity agent configuration: 

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fme-mcp-ultra": {
      "command": "E:/fme_mcp/.venv/Scripts/python.exe",
      "args": ["-m", "fme_mcp_ultra", "serve", "--transport", "stdio"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Observability & Monitoring
docs.text: fme-mcp-ultra integrates enterprise observability out-of-the-box, supporting OpenTelemetry standards, Prometheus metrics, structured JSON logs, and immutable audit trails.

docs.title: Metrics & Health Probes
docs.text:
When running in Streamable HTTP mode, the server exposes dedicated monitoring endpoints:

  • GET /healthz: Liveness probe verifying the event loop is active.
  • GET /readyz: Readiness probe testing FME Flow API or local FME Form engine connectivity.
  • GET /metrics: Standard Prometheus-formatted scrape target.

docs.title: Prometheus Metrics Exposed
docs.text: Metric Name Type Description fme_mcp_requests_total Counter Total JSON-RPC tool calls by tool name and status fme_mcp_request_duration_seconds Histogram Latency distribution of tool execution fme_mcp_active_jobs Gauge Number of concurrent active FME workspace runs fme_mcp_rate_limit_rejections_total Counter Rejected requests due to token bucket depletion fme_mcp_security_violations_total Counter SSRF, path traversal, or command injection blocks

docs.title: Structured Logging
docs.text: Logs are formatted in structured JSON conforming to the OpenTelemetry schema. Every log entry includes: - timestamp: UTC ISO-8601 with microsecond precision. - level: INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL. - correlation_id: Unique UUID per JSON-RPC request for distributed tracing across agent hops. - tool_name: Invoked MCP tool identifier. - user_id / client_id: Authenticated caller identity.

docs.title: Immutable Security Audit Trail
docs.text:
All data transformations, parameter bindings, and workspace executions are appended to an immutable append-only audit log:

{
  "timestamp": "2026-11-06T10:45:00.123456Z",
  "event_type": "TOOL_INVOCATION",
  "tool": "fme_run_workspace",
  "principal": "agent-claude-3-7",
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "duration_ms": 1420,
  "parameters_hash": "sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855",
  "client_ip": "10.244.1.42"
}

Audit records can be forwarded directly to SIEM solutions such as Splunk, Datadog, ElasticSearch, or Google Cloud Operations Suite.

docs.title: Product Roadmap
docs.text: This document outlines the strategic development milestones and feature releases planned for fme-mcp-ultra.

docs.title: Version 1.0.0 (Released — November 2026) ✅
docs.text:
• Core MCP Server: Streamable HTTP and stdio transports based on MCP specification 1.x.
  • FME 2025.2 Dual Engine:
  • Direct local FME Form execution via fme.exe CLI and fmeobjects bindings.
  • FME Flow REST API client with full authentication and workspace discovery.
  • Security Engine:
  • Path traversal guard with canonical directory allowlists.
  • Command injection guard rejecting shell metacharacters.
  • SSRF protection against private IPv4/IPv6 ranges and cloud metadata services.
  • Sensitive parameter masking and redaction.
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
  • Core Tool Suites:
  • Workspaces & Jobs execution and inspection.
  • Spatial analysis, coordinate reprojection, and geometry buffer operations.
  • Data engineering, profiling, quality validation, and schema inference.
  • Base Adresse Nationale (BAN) address geocoding and automated enrichment.
  • Distribution:
  • Open-source release under Apache 2.0.
  • Automated CI/CD GitHub Actions pipeline.
  • Published on GitHub Container Registry and GitHub Releases.

docs.title: Version 1.1.0 (Target: Q1 2027) 🔄
docs.text:
• FME 2026 Parity: Native emulation of Safe Software 2026 MCP server protocols and JSON-RPC endpoints.
  • Asynchronous Webhook Reception: Inbuilt HTTP webhook receiver for real-time FME Flow notification callbacks.
  • Enhanced Vector Indexing: Automatic semantic indexing of workspace documentation and custom transformers using local embeddings.
  • Extended Spatial Tools: Advanced 3D city model and BIM/IFC inspection tools via FME Quick Translator bindings.

docs.title: Version 1.2.0 (Target: Q2 2027) 📋
docs.text:
• Enterprise Governance Suite: Automated lineage graphing across multi-workspace data pipelines.
  • Federated MCP Gateway: Downstream routing and composition across external MCP servers (PostGIS, GeoServer, QGIS, ArcGIS Enterprise).
  • High-Throughput Batch Processing: Celery and Redis distributed job queue integration for multi-worker FME clusters.

docs.title: Security Architecture & Threat Model
docs.text: fme-mcp-ultra applies an enterprise Default-Deny security posture.

docs.title: 1. PathGuard (Directory Sandboxing)
docs.text:
• Resolves all file paths to their absolute canonical representation (os.path.realpath).
  • Enforces strict containment within FME_ALLOWED_DIRS.
  • Immediately raises PathTraversalError upon detecting .. directory traversal or null byte injection (\0).

docs.title: 2. CommandGuard (Subprocess Sandboxing)
docs.text:
• Forbids invocation of shells (shell=False is enforced across all subprocess executions).
  • Whitelists executable binaries (fme.exe, fme, python.exe).
  • Disallows shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $, >, <).

docs.title: 3. SSRF Guard (Network Defense)
docs.text:
• Pre-resolves outbound DNS hostnames.
  • Blocks calls to loopback (127.0.0.1), private networks (10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12), link-local IPs (169.254.169.254), and non-whitelisted domains.

docs.title: 4. RedactionEngine (PII & Secret Scrubbing)
docs.text: • Proactively scans stdout, stderr, and structured outputs for Bearer tokens, API credentials, email addresses, and payment card numbers, replacing them with redaction tokens before response delivery.

docs.title: 5. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
docs.text:
• Strict separation of duties:
  • platform_admin: Full access.
  • workspace_operator: Permitted to inspect and execute workspaces.
  • spatial_analyst: Vector and raster GIS operations.
  • auditor: Compliance and audit logs only.
  • read_only: Inspection and queries only.

docs.title: Tools Reference Catalogue
docs.text: A complete index of tools exposed by fme-mcp-ultra, organized by domain.

docs.title: fme_discover_workspaces
docs.text: Crawls an authorised directory to discover .fmw workspace files. - Arguments: - directory (string, optional): Base path to scan (defaults to current working directory). - recursive (boolean, optional): Recursively scan subdirectories (default true).

docs.title: fme_get_workspace
docs.text: Inspects an FME workspace without execution. - Arguments: - workspace_path (string, required): Path to the .fmw file. - Returns: Published parameters, transformers count, readers, writers, file size.

docs.title: fme_run_workspace
docs.text: Executes an FME workspace synchronously. - Arguments: - workspace_path (string, required): Path to the .fmw file. - parameters (object, optional): Published parameters key-value mapping. - log_file (string, optional): Target path for execution log. - timeout_seconds (integer, optional): Execution timeout (default 600).

docs.title: gis_reproject
docs.text: Transforms 2D coordinates between common CRS. - Arguments: - x (number, required): Longitude / Easting. - y (number, required): Latitude / Northing. - source_epsg (integer, default 4326): Source EPSG code. - target_epsg (integer, default 2154): Target EPSG code (e.g. Lambert-93 or 3857 Web Mercator).

docs.title: gis_buffer
docs.text: Generates a circular buffer polygon around a center coordinate. - Arguments: - center_lon (number, required): Longitude in degrees. - center_lat (number, required): Latitude in degrees. - radius_metres (number, required): Radius in metres. - num_points (integer, default 32): Number of perimeter vertices.

docs.title: gis_validate_geometry
docs.text: Validates structural integrity and closed polygon rings. - Arguments: - geojson_geometry (object, required): GeoJSON geometry object.

docs.title: data_read_metadata
docs.text: Inspects tabular or spatial file metadata. - Arguments: - dataset_path (string, required): Path to dataset file (CSV, GeoJSON, etc.).

docs.title: data_profile
docs.text: Computes column statistics, null counts, and completeness percentages. - Arguments: - dataset_path (string, required): Path to tabular dataset. - max_rows (integer, default 1000): Sample size ceiling.

docs.title: quality_score_dataset
docs.text: Computes overall quality score index (0–100) based on completeness. - Arguments: - dataset_path (string, required): Path to CSV dataset.
